## 1. Purpose

This module creates the common validation design used by every prediction method fitted to the real *Coffea arabica* population. The partitions are generated **before model fitting** and are reused unchanged by GBLUP and all ANN variants.

The primary validation design is a family-stratified nested cross-validation:

- **outer validation:** 5 repetitions of 5 folds, producing 25 held-out evaluations;
- **outer balance:** each assessment fold contains exactly 3 individuals from each of the 13 progenies;
- **inner validation:** 4 folds created only within the corresponding outer analysis set;
- **inner balance:** each inner assessment fold also contains exactly 3 individuals from each progeny;
- **information separation:** phenotype values and prediction-model identity do not participate in fold generation.

A complementary leave-one-family-out (LOFO) design is also stored for later evaluation of between-family generalization, but it does not replace the prespecified primary nested design.


## 2. Packages and fixed settings

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
```

```{r validation-parameters}
SEED_GLOBAL <- 20261105L
N_OUTER_REPEATS <- 5L
N_OUTER_FOLDS <- 5L
N_INNER_FOLDS <- 4L

validation_parameters <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Global seed",
    "Outer repetitions",
    "Outer folds per repetition",
    "Inner folds per outer split"
  ),
  Value = c(
    SEED_GLOBAL,
    N_OUTER_REPEATS,
    N_OUTER_FOLDS,
    N_INNER_FOLDS
  ),
  Role = c(
    "reproducible partition generation",
    "repeat held-out evaluation",
    "primary held-out assessment",
    "ANN hyperparameter selection inside outer analysis"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

validation_parameters |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Fixed real-data validation settings",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 3. Population used for partitioning

```{r validation-input}
common <- readRDS(
  "output/real/audit/preprocessed_real_common.rds"
)

ids <- rownames(common$genotype)
family <- unname(common$family[ids])

stopifnot(
  length(ids) == 195L,
  length(unique(ids)) == 195L,
  length(unique(family)) == 13L,
  all(table(family) == 15L)
)

population_summary <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Families",
    "Individuals per family",
    "Markers after common QC"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(ids),
    length(unique(family)),
    unique(as.integer(table(family))),
    ncol(common$genotype)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

population_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Population entering validation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Only individual ID, family label, and deterministic seeds are used to generate folds. The three phenotype traits remain outside partition generation.

## 4. Repeated family-stratified outer cross-validation

Each family contains 15 individuals. Within each repetition, the 15 members of each family are shuffled reproducibly and assigned as 3 individuals to each of the five outer folds. Consequently, every outer assessment set contains 39 individuals and every outer analysis set contains 156 individuals.

```{r outer-folds}
outer_assignment_list <- vector("list", N_OUTER_REPEATS)
outer_splits <- list()

for (rep_id in seq_len(N_OUTER_REPEATS)) {

  set.seed(SEED_GLOBAL + rep_id)

  fold_by_row <- integer(length(ids))

  for (family_id in unique(family)) {

    family_rows <- which(family == family_id)
    shuffled_rows <- sample(family_rows, length(family_rows), replace = FALSE)

    fold_by_row[shuffled_rows] <- rep(
      seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS),
      each = 3L
    )
  }

  outer_assignment_list[[rep_id]] <- data.frame(
    Repetition = rep_id,
    ID = ids,
    Family = family,
    OuterFold = fold_by_row,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  for (outer_fold in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {

    split_id <- sprintf("R%02d_F%02d", rep_id, outer_fold)

    assessment_index <- which(fold_by_row == outer_fold)
    analysis_index <- which(fold_by_row != outer_fold)

    outer_splits[[split_id]] <- list(
      split_id = split_id,
      repetition = rep_id,
      outer_fold = outer_fold,
      analysis_ids = ids[analysis_index],
      assessment_ids = ids[assessment_index]
    )
  }
}

outer_assignments <- do.call(rbind, outer_assignment_list)
rownames(outer_assignments) <- NULL

outer_assignments$SplitID <- sprintf(
  "R%02d_F%02d",
  outer_assignments$Repetition,
  outer_assignments$OuterFold
)
```

```{r outer-checks}
outer_sizes <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(outer_splits, function(x) {
    data.frame(
      SplitID = x$split_id,
      Analysis_N = length(x$analysis_ids),
      Assessment_N = length(x$assessment_ids),
      Overlap_N = length(intersect(x$analysis_ids, x$assessment_ids)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

outer_family_balance <- all(
  vapply(
    outer_splits,
    function(x) {
      all(table(family[match(x$assessment_ids, ids)]) == 3L)
    },
    logical(1)
  )
)

outer_coverage <- all(
  vapply(
    seq_len(N_OUTER_REPEATS),
    function(rep_id) {
      split_ids <- sprintf(
        "R%02d_F%02d",
        rep_id,
        seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)
      )

      assessed <- unlist(
        lapply(outer_splits[split_ids], `[[`, "assessment_ids"),
        use.names = FALSE
      )

      identical(sort(assessed), sort(ids)) &&
        all(table(assessed) == 1L)
    },
    logical(1)
  )
)

outer_contract <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "25 outer splits",
    "156 analysis individuals per split",
    "39 assessment individuals per split",
    "No analysis-assessment overlap",
    "Exactly 3 assessment individuals per family",
    "Every individual assessed exactly once per repetition"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    length(outer_splits) == 25L,
    all(outer_sizes$Analysis_N == 156L),
    all(outer_sizes$Assessment_N == 39L),
    all(outer_sizes$Overlap_N == 0L),
    outer_family_balance,
    outer_coverage
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

outer_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Outer validation contract",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(all(outer_contract$Passed))
```

The coverage check explicitly removes list-generated names before comparison, avoiding the false negative that can occur when `unlist()` names are compared with an unnamed vector.

## 5. Nested inner cross-validation

Each outer analysis set contains 12 individuals from every family. Those 12 individuals are divided into four inner folds of 3 individuals per family. Thus every inner assessment set contains 39 individuals and every inner analysis set contains 117 individuals.

The outer assessment individuals never participate in inner partition generation.

```{r inner-folds}
inner_assignments_list <- list()
inner_splits <- setNames(
  vector("list", length(outer_splits)),
  names(outer_splits)
)

for (split_id in names(outer_splits)) {

  outer_split <- outer_splits[[split_id]]

  rep_id <- outer_split$repetition
  outer_fold <- outer_split$outer_fold

  outer_analysis_ids <- outer_split$analysis_ids
  outer_analysis_index <- match(outer_analysis_ids, ids)
  outer_analysis_family <- family[outer_analysis_index]

  set.seed(
    SEED_GLOBAL +
      100000L +
      rep_id * 100L +
      outer_fold
  )

  inner_fold_by_row <- integer(length(outer_analysis_ids))

  for (family_id in unique(outer_analysis_family)) {

    family_rows <- which(outer_analysis_family == family_id)
    shuffled_rows <- sample(family_rows, length(family_rows), replace = FALSE)

    inner_fold_by_row[shuffled_rows] <- rep(
      seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS),
      each = 3L
    )
  }

  inner_assignments_list[[split_id]] <- data.frame(
    SplitID = split_id,
    Repetition = rep_id,
    OuterFold = outer_fold,
    ID = outer_analysis_ids,
    Family = outer_analysis_family,
    InnerFold = inner_fold_by_row,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  current_inner_splits <- setNames(
    vector("list", N_INNER_FOLDS),
    paste0("I", seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS))
  )

  for (inner_fold in seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS)) {

    assessment_rows <- which(inner_fold_by_row == inner_fold)
    analysis_rows <- which(inner_fold_by_row != inner_fold)

    current_inner_splits[[paste0("I", inner_fold)]] <- list(
      split_id = split_id,
      inner_fold = inner_fold,
      analysis_ids = outer_analysis_ids[analysis_rows],
      assessment_ids = outer_analysis_ids[assessment_rows]
    )
  }

  inner_splits[[split_id]] <- current_inner_splits
}

inner_assignments <- do.call(rbind, inner_assignments_list)
rownames(inner_assignments) <- NULL
```

```{r inner-checks}
inner_size_rows <- list()
row_id <- 1L

for (split_id in names(inner_splits)) {
  for (inner_name in names(inner_splits[[split_id]])) {

    x <- inner_splits[[split_id]][[inner_name]]

    inner_size_rows[[row_id]] <- data.frame(
      SplitID = split_id,
      InnerFold = x$inner_fold,
      Analysis_N = length(x$analysis_ids),
      Assessment_N = length(x$assessment_ids),
      Overlap_N = length(intersect(x$analysis_ids, x$assessment_ids)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    row_id <- row_id + 1L
  }
}

inner_sizes <- do.call(rbind, inner_size_rows)
rownames(inner_sizes) <- NULL

inner_family_balance <- all(
  vapply(
    names(inner_splits),
    function(split_id) {
      all(
        vapply(
          inner_splits[[split_id]],
          function(x) {
            assessment_family <- family[match(x$assessment_ids, ids)]
            all(table(assessment_family) == 3L)
          },
          logical(1)
        )
      )
    },
    logical(1)
  )
)

outer_leakage <- any(
  vapply(
    names(outer_splits),
    function(split_id) {

      outer_assessment <- outer_splits[[split_id]]$assessment_ids

      any(
        vapply(
          inner_splits[[split_id]],
          function(x) {
            length(
              intersect(
                outer_assessment,
                c(x$analysis_ids, x$assessment_ids)
              )
            ) > 0L
          },
          logical(1)
        )
      )
    },
    logical(1)
  )
)

inner_contract <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "100 inner splits",
    "117 inner-analysis individuals per split",
    "39 inner-assessment individuals per split",
    "No inner analysis-assessment overlap",
    "Exactly 3 inner-assessment individuals per family",
    "No outer-assessment individual appears in inner validation"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    nrow(inner_sizes) == 100L,
    all(inner_sizes$Analysis_N == 117L),
    all(inner_sizes$Assessment_N == 39L),
    all(inner_sizes$Overlap_N == 0L),
    inner_family_balance,
    !outer_leakage
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

inner_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Nested inner-validation contract",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(all(inner_contract$Passed))
```

## 6. Complementary leave-one-family-out design

The primary nested cross-validation estimates predictive performance when all 13 progenies are represented in model development. A complementary LOFO design is stored separately to evaluate the more demanding setting in which one complete progeny is absent from training.

```{r lofo-design}
family_levels <- sort(unique(family))

lofo_splits <- setNames(
  vector("list", length(family_levels)),
  family_levels
)

lofo_assignments <- data.frame(
  ID = ids,
  Family = family,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (family_id in family_levels) {

  assessment_ids <- ids[family == family_id]
  analysis_ids <- ids[family != family_id]

  lofo_splits[[family_id]] <- list(
    held_out_family = family_id,
    analysis_ids = analysis_ids,
    assessment_ids = assessment_ids
  )
}

lofo_sizes <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(lofo_splits, function(x) {
    data.frame(
      Held_out_family = x$held_out_family,
      Analysis_N = length(x$analysis_ids),
      Assessment_N = length(x$assessment_ids),
      Overlap_N = length(intersect(x$analysis_ids, x$assessment_ids)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

stopifnot(
  length(lofo_splits) == 13L,
  all(lofo_sizes$Analysis_N == 180L),
  all(lofo_sizes$Assessment_N == 15L),
  all(lofo_sizes$Overlap_N == 0L)
)

lofo_sizes |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Complementary leave-one-family-out splits",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 9. Save the common validation object

```{r save-validation-outputs, include=FALSE}
cv_design <- list(
  dataset = "real",
  seed_global = SEED_GLOBAL,
  n_outer_repeats = N_OUTER_REPEATS,
  n_outer_folds = N_OUTER_FOLDS,
  n_inner_folds = N_INNER_FOLDS,
  ids = ids,
  family = setNames(family, ids),
  outer_assignments = outer_assignments,
  outer_splits = outer_splits,
  inner_assignments = inner_assignments,
  inner_splits = inner_splits,
  lofo_splits = lofo_splits,
  checks = list(
    outer_contract = outer_contract,
    inner_contract = inner_contract,
    outer_family_balance = outer_family_balance,
    outer_coverage = outer_coverage,
    outer_leakage = outer_leakage
  )
)

saveRDS(
  cv_design,
  "output/real/validation/real_cv_design.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  outer_assignments,
  "output/real/validation/real_outer_assignments.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  inner_assignments,
  "output/real/validation/real_inner_assignments.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  lofo_sizes,
  "output/real/validation/real_lofo_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  design_summary,
  "output/real/validation/real_validation_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 10. Frozen validation contract

The primary real-data comparison is based on the same 25 family-stratified outer assessments for GBLUP and every ANN variant. ANN hyperparameter selection is restricted to the corresponding 100 inner splits; outer-assessment phenotypes remain unavailable during model development.

The complementary 13-fold LOFO design is stored independently and can later be used to quantify generalization to progenies absent from model training without changing the primary model-comparison contract.
